title: Crochet Beanie for Beginners | Sara Rain Crochet
description: Learn how to crochet a cozy beginner beanie with a simple round crown, comfortable fit, and optional pom-pom finish.

title: Crochet Baby Blanket
description: A soft, beginner-friendly crochet baby blanket with a simple shell texture, gentle shaping, and a scalloped border.
materials: DK baby yarn, 5.5 mm hook, scissors, tapestry needle
intro: Start with a soft washable yarn and a foundation width that feels useful rather than oversized. The sample method below uses a repeatable shell texture so the blanket grows predictably while staying relaxed and cozy.
steps: Choose a foundation chain that gives the finished blanket the width you want, keeping the stitch repeat consistent.
Work the first setup row evenly, then build the shell pattern across each row.
Keep the first and last stitch easy to see with a marker.
Continue until the blanket reaches the desired length, then add a simple border and scalloped edge.
checkpoint: Check the width after every few rows. The edges should remain parallel, and each shell should sit in the same rhythm as the row before it. If the fabric starts narrowing, count the first and last stitches before continuing.
troubleshooting: If the shells look crowded, loosen your tension or use a slightly larger hook. If the fabric feels floppy and holes are larger than expected, tighten your tension or test a smaller hook. Always make a small swatch before committing to a large blanket.
finishing: Weave in all ends securely on the back. Add the scalloped border slowly around the corners so the edge does not ruffle. Shape the blanket flat while damp only if the yarn label allows it.
variations: Try two neutral shades, a soft striped sequence, or a single color with a contrasting border. The same shell rhythm also works for stroller blankets and lap blankets.
care: Wash and dry according to the yarn label. Store the finished blanket folded loosely so the border keeps its shape.

title: Crochet Baby Booties
description: A sweet beginner crochet baby booties tutorial using a small oval sole, shaped upper, toe decreases, and a simple tie.
materials: Soft baby yarn, 3.5 mm hook, tapestry needle, scissors, optional ribbon
intro: Baby booties are small, but accurate counting matters. Work both booties from the same notes so the pair matches in length, height, and toe shaping.
steps: Begin with an oval sole, working around both sides of the foundation chain.
Build the upper with even rounds, then concentrate decreases around the toe so the front curves naturally.
Finish the ankle and make the second bootie using the same number of rounds.
checkpoint: Lay the two soles together before shaping the uppers. After the toe round, both booties should have matching openings and similar side height.
troubleshooting: If the sole curls, check your stitch placement around the rounded ends. If the toe looks too pointed, spread the decreases over more stitches. Avoid tight ribbon ties and follow safe-use guidance for baby items.
finishing: Weave in ends inside the bootie and gently shape the toe. Add a soft decorative tie only if it can be secured safely and comfortably.
variations: Make a matching pair in two colors, add a simple contrast cuff, or use the sole as the base for a slightly taller slipper.
care: Follow the yarn label for washing. Check the finished booties for loose ends before every use.

title: Crochet Beanie for Beginners
description: Make a cozy beginner beanie with a simple round crown, even body, and optional pom-pom finish.
materials: Worsted yarn, 6 mm hook, stitch markers, scissors, optional pom-pom
intro: A beanie is a useful first wearable because small changes in hook size and tension are easy to see. Measure the head before choosing the final circumference.
steps: Start at the crown and increase evenly until the circle reaches the intended crown width.
Work the body without increases, checking the depth against the wearer.
Finish with a firm but comfortable edge and add a pom-pom if desired.
checkpoint: Measure the crown flat without stretching it. Try the hat on before finishing the brim so you can adjust depth while the top is still easy to change.
troubleshooting: If the crown becomes wavy, there are too many increases. If it forms a cone, add increases more gradually. If the brim is tight, change hook size rather than forcing the fabric to stretch.
finishing: Fasten off with a generous tail and weave it through several stitches. Secure a pom-pom from inside the hat with multiple passes if you use one.
variations: Use stripes, a folded brim, a contrast crown, or a small embroidered motif. Make a child and adult version by recalculating circumference from measurements.
care: Wash according to the yarn label and reshape the hat while damp if recommended.

title: Crochet Bookmark
description: A slim crochet bookmark with a delicate lace section, tassel, blocking, and gift-ready finishing.
materials: Thin cotton yarn, 3 mm hook, scissors, yarn needle
intro: A bookmark is a great scrap-yarn project: it is quick, flat, and gives you a place to practice even chains and openwork.
steps: Chain to the length you want, then work a narrow lace-style stitch pattern back and forth.
Keep the side edges straight by checking the first and last stitch of each row.
Finish with a small tassel and block the bookmark flat.
checkpoint: Place the bookmark inside a book while it is still untrimmed to check the length. The finished piece should lie flat without pulling the spine or protruding too far.
troubleshooting: If the edges wave, reduce tension changes between chains and stitches. If the bookmark twists, block it gently and check that turning chains are consistent.
finishing: Weave in the working end, trim the tassel evenly, and block the piece flat if the yarn permits.
variations: Try a contrast tassel, a tiny flower at the end, or a longer version for journals.
care: Keep it dry and wash gently if the fiber allows. Store it flat inside a favorite book.

title: Crochet Bucket Hat
description: A beginner bucket hat with a rounded crown, straight side depth, widening brim, and optional structured edge.
materials: Bulky cotton yarn, 5.5 mm hook, stitch markers, measuring tape
intro: Cotton is useful for a bucket hat because it gives the fabric enough structure to hold the brim. Measure the head circumference before starting.
steps: Crochet the crown in rounds, increasing evenly until it matches the top-of-head measurement.
Work the side section without increases, then widen the brim over several rounds.
Finish with a final edge that stabilizes the shape.
checkpoint: Check crown width before adding depth. Try the hat on after the side section and again halfway through the brim.
troubleshooting: A wavy brim usually means increases were added too quickly. A brim that curls upward needs more width or a different hook. If the crown cups too sharply, spread increases across more rounds.
finishing: Weave in ends and steam or lightly shape only if the cotton care instructions permit it. A firm final round can help the brim keep its line.
variations: Add stripes, a contrast brim, a tiny flower, or a simple embroidered initial.
care: Spot clean or wash according to the yarn label. Dry flat or reshape over a bowl if recommended.

title: Crochet Cardigan
description: A beginner-friendly cardigan construction using a back panel, two front panels, simple sleeves, and a button band.
materials: Worsted yarn, 5.5 mm hook, scissors, tapestry needle, buttons
intro: A simple panel construction makes a cardigan easier to adjust because each piece can be measured before assembly. Use the wearer’s chest and arm measurements rather than relying only on a generic size.
steps: Make the back panel first, then crochet two matching front panels.
Work sleeves as rectangles or tapered pieces, seam them carefully, and attach them to the arm openings.
Add a button band along the fronts and finish with buttons.
checkpoint: Lay the front panels over the back before seaming. Shoulder widths should match, and sleeve openings should be positioned symmetrically.
troubleshooting: If the cardigan pulls at the shoulders, recheck panel width and seam allowance. If sleeves twist, mark the top center before attaching them. If the front edges ripple, reduce extra stitches in the button band.
finishing: Block each panel before assembly when the yarn allows it. Sew buttons firmly and weave all ends between fabric layers.
variations: Try a cropped length, longer sleeves, contrast cuffs, or a simple belt. The same panel method can become a vest by omitting sleeves.
care: Wash according to the yarn label and store flat to protect the shoulders and button band.

title: Crochet Crop Top
description: A simple cotton crochet crop top with measured panels, joined shoulders, side seams, and adjustable ties.
materials: Cotton yarn, 5 mm hook, measuring tape, scissors, stitch markers
intro: A crop top needs accurate measurements more than complicated stitches. Measure bust, underbust, and desired length, then make a small swatch to understand stretch.
steps: Work the front and back panels to the measured width, keeping rows even.
Join the shoulders, seam the sides, then add an edging and ties.
Try the top on before securing the ties permanently.
checkpoint: Check the panel width against the body before joining. The side seams should sit comfortably without pulling, and the neckline should lie flat.
troubleshooting: If the top stretches too much, use a firmer stitch or smaller hook. If it feels rigid, loosen tension or use a more flexible stitch. Always consider the stretch after washing.
finishing: Weave in ends on the inside and reinforce tie attachment points with extra stitches.
variations: Make a striped version, add a scalloped edge, or turn it into a longer tank by extending the panels.
care: Wash according to the cotton label and dry flat to help preserve the shape.

title: Crochet Dog Bandana
description: A beginner pet bandana worked as a measured triangle with an edging and comfortable neck tie.
materials: Medium cotton yarn, 4.5 mm hook, scissors, yarn needle
intro: Measure around the pet’s neck and choose a finished bandana width that leaves room for movement. The sample approach is intentionally simple so you can adjust the triangle easily.
steps: Start at the top edge and decrease toward the point, or build a triangle from the point outward depending on your preferred construction.
Add an even edging and a tie or casing that sits comfortably around the neck.
checkpoint: Try the bandana on before trimming the ties. It should rest comfortably without pressing into the throat or restricting movement.
troubleshooting: If the triangle twists, check that decreases are centered. If the tie feels bulky, use a narrower cord or work a casing instead.
finishing: Weave in ends thoroughly and inspect the fabric for loose loops before use.
variations: Make seasonal colors, a small embroidered initial, or a matching human-and-pet set.
care: Hand wash gently and dry flat when recommended. Inspect regularly for wear.

title: Crochet Ear Warmer
description: A quick chunky ear warmer with a flat rectangle, a gathered or seamed center, and a comfortable stretch.
materials: Chunky or wool-blend yarn, 5.5 mm hook, tapestry needle, scissors
intro: The key to an ear warmer is stretch. Measure the head and make the band slightly smaller than the circumference so the fabric can hold gently without squeezing.
steps: Chain to the desired height, work rows until the rectangle wraps around the head, then seam the short ends.
Add a twist or gather at the center if you want a more decorative shape.
checkpoint: Wrap the unfinished rectangle around the head to check stretch before seaming. The join should sit comfortably behind or beside the ear.
troubleshooting: If the band is too loose, reduce the length rather than pulling it tighter during seaming. If it is too tight, add rows or use a larger hook.
finishing: Hide the seam inside the center gather if using a twist. Weave in ends securely and shape the front edge.
variations: Try a simple twist, a contrast stripe, or a button detail.
care: Follow the yarn label for washing and reshape while damp if recommended.

title: Crochet Fingerless Gloves
description: Simple fingerless gloves with a wrist-to-hand tube, a thumb opening, and a neat cuff.
materials: Worsted yarn, 5 mm hook, stitch marker, tapestry needle
intro: Fingerless gloves are forgiving because the fingers remain open, but the wrist fit still matters. Measure wrist and hand circumference before choosing the starting size.
steps: Work a tube around the wrist and hand, checking circumference as you go.
Mark a thumb opening, then continue the hand section and finish with a clean cuff or edging.
Make the second glove from the same measurements.
checkpoint: Compare both gloves after the wrist section. The thumb opening should align with the hand rather than sitting too close to the palm edge.
troubleshooting: If the glove spirals, check whether you are joining rounds consistently. If the thumb opening stretches too far, reinforce the surrounding stitches with an extra round.
finishing: Weave in ends along the inside of the cuff and around the thumb opening.
variations: Use two colors, a ribbed cuff, or a simple textured stitch.
care: Wash according to the yarn label and reshape flat.

title: Crochet Headband
description: A beginner headband made from a simple rectangle with stretch, a center twist, and a clean seam.
materials: Medium-weight yarn, 5 mm hook, scissors, yarn needle
intro: This project is built around one rectangle, so it is easy to measure and adjust. The important part is getting the stretch right before joining the ends.
steps: Chain to the headband height, then work single crochet rows until the rectangle wraps comfortably around the head.
Check stretch, add the center twist, seam the short ends, and weave in the tails.
checkpoint: Stretch the unfinished band gently around the head. It should recover without leaving a large gap.
troubleshooting: If the band grows too long, shorten the foundation or remove a few rows. If it feels rigid, loosen tension or choose a softer yarn.
finishing: Keep the center twist symmetrical and hide the seam inside the back layer. Weave ends through several rows.
variations: Try a bow, a contrast center, or a textured stitch while keeping the same rectangle construction.
care: Wash and dry according to the yarn label.

title: Crochet Keychain
description: A tiny stuffed crochet keychain made from a small amigurumi shape, stuffing, and a secure keyring attachment.
materials: Worsted cotton yarn, 3.5 mm hook, keyring and clasp, polyfill, tapestry needle
intro: Small keychains are excellent scrap-yarn projects. Keep the stitches dense enough that stuffing cannot easily show through the fabric.
steps: Start a small round shape with a magic ring, increase to the widest point, work several even rounds, then decrease and add a little stuffing.
Close the opening, weave the tail securely, and attach the keyring through a reinforced loop.
checkpoint: Before attaching hardware, gently pull the hanging loop to test its strength. The finished shape should be firm without being overstuffed.
troubleshooting: If stuffing shows, use a smaller hook or tighter tension. If the opening puckers badly, reduce stuffing before closing.
finishing: Reinforce the hardware loop with multiple passes of yarn. Trim ends only after the attachment has been tested.
variations: Make hearts, fruit, tiny animals, or letter charms. Create a color-matched set for bags or gifts.
care: Keep the keychain dry and inspect the hardware periodically.

title: Crochet Laptop Sleeve
description: A protective crochet laptop sleeve with a measured rectangle, flap, button closure, and neat finishing.
materials: Chunky cotton yarn, 6 mm hook, wooden button, tapestry needle
intro: Measure the laptop including any case you plan to keep on it. The sleeve should fit snugly but should never require force to insert or remove the device.
steps: Make a rectangle wide enough for the laptop and long enough to fold over the top.
Work the body in even rows, fold the bottom and sides into a sleeve, seam securely, then add a flap and button loop.
checkpoint: Test the fit before final seaming. The laptop should slide in smoothly and sit below the flap without stretching the fabric excessively.
troubleshooting: If the sleeve is too tight, add width rather than relying on stretch. If it is too loose, reduce the foundation width. Reinforce corners because they receive the most movement.
finishing: Sew the button securely and weave ends into multiple directions. Avoid hard protrusions on the inside that could scratch the device.
variations: Add a lining, contrast flap, stripes, or a carrying strap.
care: Spot clean or wash according to the yarn label and let it dry completely before storing electronics.

title: Crochet Mug Cozy
description: A quick mug cozy that measures around the cup, works flat in single crochet, and closes with a button and loop.
materials: Worsted cotton yarn, 5 mm hook, wooden button, yarn needle
intro: Measure the mug’s circumference and height before starting. Leave the handle area unobstructed and avoid making the cozy so tight that it cannot slide off.
steps: Chain to the cozy height, then work rows of single crochet until the fabric wraps around the mug.
Add a button loop at one end, sew the button to the other end, and test the closure.
checkpoint: Slip the unfinished cozy around the mug. It should sit securely while leaving the handle free and allowing the mug to be removed easily.
troubleshooting: If the cozy rides upward, reduce the height or add a stabilizing edge. If the button loop stretches, shorten it and reinforce its base.
finishing: Weave in ends, sew the button with several passes, and check that no yarn tails sit near the drink opening.
variations: Make seasonal colors, initials, stripes, or a matching coaster.
care: Remove before washing the mug. Wash the cozy according to the yarn label and dry fully.

title: Crochet Pencil Bag
description: A simple crochet pencil bag with a rectangular body, zipper, neat side seams, and optional tassels.
materials: Cotton yarn, 4 mm hook, 7-inch zipper, yarn needle, stitch markers
intro: This version uses the same practical construction as a small pouch: crochet a rectangle, prepare the zipper, close the sides, and add decorative tassels if desired.
steps: Work the rectangular body in even rows, keeping the edges straight.
Prepare the zipper with careful alignment, sew or crochet it into place, then close the side seams and add tassels.
checkpoint: Place the zipper along the unfinished top edge before attaching it. The teeth should remain straight and the two sides should meet evenly at the corners.
troubleshooting: If the zipper puckers, loosen the attachment stitches and realign it before sewing the sides. If the pouch twists, check that both short edges have the same row count.
finishing: Secure zipper ends, weave in all yarn tails, and trim tassels evenly.
variations: Use color blocks, a contrast zipper, initials, or a lined interior.
care: Empty the pouch before washing and follow the yarn label.

title: Crochet Pet Sweater
description: A measured beginner pet sweater using simple panels, leg openings, and a comfortable neck finish.
materials: Worsted yarn, 5 mm hook, measuring tape, scissors, stitch markers
intro: Measure the pet’s neck, chest, back length, and leg spacing. A sweater should allow free movement and should never be tight around the throat or chest.
steps: Make the body to the measured chest width, create leg openings with controlled shaping, and continue toward the back.
Finish the neck and belly edges with a comfortable border.
checkpoint: Try the sweater on during construction rather than waiting until the end. Check the chest, shoulder movement, and leg openings.
troubleshooting: If the body twists, compare both sides for equal stitch counts. If an opening feels tight, add width rather than stretching the fabric.
finishing: Weave in ends securely and inspect all seams. Remove loose decorative pieces that could become a hazard.
variations: Make a hoodless version, contrast trim, or a simple stripe.
care: Wash according to the yarn label and inspect seams regularly.

title: Crochet Pillow Cover
description: A textured crochet pillow cover built from front and back panels with a simple closure and clean corners.
materials: Chunky yarn, 6 mm hook, tapestry needle, pillow insert
intro: Measure the pillow insert first. Crochet panels should be slightly smaller or equal to the insert depending on how snug you want the finished cover.
steps: Work the front panel in an even stitch pattern.
Make a matching back panel, leaving an overlap or opening for the insert.
Seam three sides, insert the pillow, and close the final edge with buttons or a neat seam.
checkpoint: Lay both panels together before seaming. Corners should align and the opening should be large enough to insert the pillow without stretching the fabric.
troubleshooting: If corners flare, reduce extra stitches at the ends of rows. If the cover is loose, reduce panel width rather than tightening the seam.
finishing: Weave in ends inside the cover and reinforce button areas with extra yarn.
variations: Try a checkerboard texture, contrast back panel, envelope closure, or seasonal front motif.
care: Remove the insert before washing and follow the yarn label.

title: Crochet Placemat Set
description: A beginner placemat set using cotton yarn, even rows, a simple border, and consistent sizing across the set.
materials: Cotton yarn, 5 mm hook, stitch markers, scissors
intro: Cotton makes a practical placemat because it handles everyday use and gives clear stitch definition. Make one placemat first and use it as the sizing master for the rest.
steps: Chain to the desired table width, work the body in even rows, then add a border around all four sides.
Repeat using the same row count and tension for a matched set.
checkpoint: Stack finished placemats and compare their dimensions. The corners should sit flat and the borders should match in width.
troubleshooting: If the edges ripple, check whether the border adds too many stitches. If corners cup, add a corner stitch or small chain space.
finishing: Weave in ends on the back, block flat if suitable, and trim any uneven border loops.
variations: Use seasonal colors, two-tone borders, or a subtle stripe sequence.
care: Wash according to the cotton label and dry flat when recommended.

title: Crochet Plant Hanger
description: A beginner crochet plant hanger with a sturdy basket base, long support strands, and a wooden or metal ring.
materials: Cotton cord or yarn, 5 mm hook, wooden or metal ring, scissors
intro: Choose a small lightweight pot for the first version and make sure the yarn or cord is strong enough for the finished load. The crochet basket should support the pot without stretching excessively.
steps: Work a round base that fits beneath the pot, build the basket sides upward, then create several evenly spaced support strands that gather at a ring.
Test the empty hanger before adding a plant.
checkpoint: Place the pot inside and check that the base remains centered. Pull each support strand gently to make sure the load is shared evenly.
troubleshooting: If the basket stretches too much, use a firmer cord or smaller hook. If the hanger tilts, rebalance the support strands before hanging it.
finishing: Secure every strand at the ring with multiple passes. Keep knots and ends away from the pot edge and inspect before use.
variations: Try a longer hanger, a double-ring design, or a contrast basket.
care: Keep the hanger dry when possible and inspect it for wear before rehanging a plant.

title: Crochet Scrunchie
description: A quick crochet scrunchie worked around a hair elastic with a ruffled finish and hidden join.
materials: Cotton or velvet yarn, 4–5 mm hook, hair elastic, scissors, tapestry needle
intro: The elastic is the foundation of this project. Keep the first round snug enough to cover it without making the elastic stiff.
steps: Chain or single crochet around the elastic, work the first round evenly, add a ruffle increase round, then close the round and weave the tail around the base.
Fluff the ruffles to finish.
checkpoint: Stretch the scrunchie gently after the first round. The elastic should still have room to contract and the crochet should cover it evenly.
troubleshooting: If the ruffle is too flat, add more increase stitches. If it becomes bulky, reduce the increase frequency. Make sure the elastic remains flexible.
finishing: Hide the join inside the ruffle and weave the tail around several stitches.
variations: Use velvet yarn for a plush look, two colors for stripes, or a tiny bow for a gift set.
care: Wash gently according to the yarn label and let dry fully before use.

title: Crochet Cozy Socks
description: A cozy beginner sock construction with a rounded toe, foot tube, heel section, ankle, and ribbed cuff.
materials: Soft sock yarn, 3.5 mm hook, stitch markers, scissors, yarn needle
intro: Crochet socks depend on fit. Measure foot length, widest foot circumference, and ankle circumference before choosing the starting stitch count.
steps: Begin at the toe with a magic ring and increase to the foot width.
Work the foot length, shape a heel section, continue up the ankle, and finish with a ribbed cuff.
Make the second sock from the same measurements.
checkpoint: Try the sock on after the foot and again after the heel. The heel should sit securely without pulling the fabric forward.
troubleshooting: If the sock twists, check stitch counts and round joins. If the heel feels shallow, add rows before continuing the ankle.
finishing: Weave in ends inside the sock and smooth the heel seam so it does not rub.
variations: Try ankle stripes, contrast cuffs, or a simple textured foot.
care: Wash according to the yarn label and dry flat when recommended.

title: Crochet Sunglasses Case
description: A slim crochet glasses case with a rectangular body, button closure, and protective snug fit.
materials: Cotton yarn, 4 mm hook, yarn needle, button
intro: Measure the sunglasses including their widest points. The case should protect the glasses without forcing the frames into a tight opening.
steps: Work a rectangle to the measured width, fold it into a sleeve, seam the sides, and add a flap with a button closure.
Test the glasses inside before trimming the final ends.
checkpoint: Slide the glasses in and out several times. The opening should be easy to use while the closure keeps the case shut.
troubleshooting: If the case is too tight, add width or use a larger hook. If the flap is too short, add rows before sewing the button.
finishing: Reinforce the button and flap loop with extra stitches and weave the ends inside the seam area.
variations: Add a contrast lining, a wrist loop, stripes, or a small flower.
care: Keep the case dry and wash according to the yarn label.

title: Crochet Table Runner
description: A long beginner table runner with a measured foundation, lace-style center, scalloped border, and blocking.
materials: Cotton yarn, 5.5 mm hook, scissors, measuring tape
intro: Measure the table before choosing the runner length. Leave enough uncovered table at each end for the look you want.
steps: Chain the measured length, work a lace-style pattern across the center, repeat rows until the runner reaches the desired width, then add a scalloped border.
Block flat if suitable.
checkpoint: Lay the runner on the table before finishing the border. Check that the length is centered and the edges remain straight.
troubleshooting: If the runner becomes wider on one end, compare the first and last stitches of each row. If the lace ripples, check tension and repeat counts.
finishing: Weave in all ends, add the border evenly around corners, and block flat according to the fiber.
variations: Use a contrast border, seasonal stripes, or a narrower version for a console table.
care: Wash according to the cotton label and dry flat.

title: Crochet Tote Bag
description: A practical crochet tote bag with a sturdy rectangular body, handles, optional lining, and everyday finishing.
materials: Cotton or chunky yarn, 6 mm hook, stitch markers, scissors, tapestry needle, optional lining fabric
intro: Choose a yarn that can handle repeated use and decide the finished bag dimensions before starting. Cotton gives a stable everyday fabric.
steps: Work the base first, then build the body upward in even rounds or rows.
Shape the top edge, make two matching handles, attach them securely, and add a lining if desired.
checkpoint: Place the unfinished bag on a flat surface to check symmetry. Test the handle length over your shoulder before sewing them permanently.
troubleshooting: If the bag stretches too much, use tighter tension or a firmer stitch. If handles pull away, reinforce their attachment across several rows.
finishing: Weave ends into the inside, reinforce stress points, and sew in a lining without pulling the crochet fabric out of shape.
variations: Add pockets, a contrast handle, stripes, or a magnetic-style closure if suitable.
care: Wash according to the yarn label and dry flat. Avoid overloading the bag.

title: Crochet Wall Hanging
description: A beginner tapestry-style wall hanging with a textured center, fringe, and wooden dowel finish.
materials: Cotton or chunky cream yarn, 5 mm hook, wooden dowel, scissors, tapestry needle
intro: Keep the first wall hanging small so you can practice even edges and fringe spacing. A wooden dowel makes a simple, clean display finish.
steps: Crochet a rectangular panel in your chosen stitch pattern, add a neat top edge, attach it to the dowel with yarn loops, and finish the bottom with evenly spaced fringe.
checkpoint: Lay the panel flat before adding fringe. Check the top edge is straight and the dowel loops are evenly spaced.
troubleshooting: If the panel leans, compare row counts and edge stitches. If fringe looks uneven, trim only after all pieces are attached.
finishing: Weave in ends on the back and secure the dowel loops with multiple passes. Comb and trim fringe gently.
variations: Try a geometric stripe, a small plant motif, longer fringe, or a contrast dowel.
care: Dust gently and avoid soaking the wooden dowel. Follow the yarn care label for deeper cleaning.

title: Easy Crochet Baby Blanket Pattern for Beginners | Sara Rain Crochet
description: Learn how to crochet a soft beginner-friendly baby blanket using DK yarn, a 5.5mm hook, an easy shell stitch, and a simple scalloped border.

title: Easy Crochet Baby Booties
description: Learn how to crochet soft baby booties with an easy oval sole, simple upper rounds, and gentle toe shaping. A beginner-friendly crochet baby booties pattern.
